- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:569-674 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The check-run path uses `CHECK_RUN_ID` (from `github.event.check_run.id`, passed at `internal-check-failure-triage.yml:30`) as the Actions job ID in `POST actions/jobs/<CHECK_RUN_ID>/rerun` (`check_failure_triage.sh:673-674`), and also compares it with the `/job/<id>` parsed from `details_url` (`rd_job`) at `check_failure_triage.sh:569-570`.
  WHY: Both reviewers rated this MAJOR. They say the check-run ID and the Actions job ID can differ, citing the fixture at `tests/test_review_final_ci.py:426-428`; if they differ, the guard skips the rerun, or the POST hits the wrong ID or returns a 404 and triage carries on. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash explicitly rejected this: for Actions check runs the two IDs are the same, the guard at 569-570 enforces `rd_job == CHECK_RUN_ID`, and the fixture is a stub.
- .github/workflows/check_failure_triage.yml:650 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `CHECK_TRIAGE_RUN_TITLE` expression gates on `github.event_name == 'workflow_run'` inside a reusable workflow that only has a `workflow_call` trigger, so it always evaluates to `''`. The script (scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:1303-1307) then falls back to `CHECK_NAME` = `CI`, which never matches `^CI \[pr:N\]…$`.
  WHY: The reviewer rated this MAJOR. Inside a called reusable workflow `github.event_name` is `workflow_call`, so the `final_ci_repair_owns` skip never fires and duplicate triage issues are still filed. The tests at tests/test_check_failure_triage_owned_failures.py:191-209 only string-match the expression, and one of them asserts that the wrapper passes no `run_title:`, which locks in the broken wiring.
- scripts/check_failure_triage.sh:945-950 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The `base_tracked` file decision still logs `reason=failed_jobs_differ` when the PR run has no failed jobs (all of its non-success jobs are `cancelled` or `action_required`).
  WHY: The reviewer rated this NIT. Filing still happens, so the behaviour is safe, but the log reason is misleading; it should be `reason=no_failed_jobs`. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3 and z-ai_glm-5_3-flash raised the same point as hardening suggestions only.
- scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py:344-391 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: New comments say "keep the bounds and checks of both copies in sync", but the shell gate's jq validation (scripts/check_failure_triage.sh lines 613-618) checks neither `.id` nor `.name`, unlike `list_run_jobs()` (lines 368-372). An annotations page of 100 or more items also gets a different skip reason (Python line 391 vs shell line 652).
  WHY: The reviewer rated this NIT. Behaviour is unchanged apart from the skip-reason token, but the comments are misleading and the issue's goal (f) asks for "no remaining drift".
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  WHY: Behaviour is unchanged apart from the skip-reason token, but the comments will mislead the next person who edits either copy. Suggested fix: add `(.id | type) == "number" and (.name | type) == "string"` to the jq all() at lines 615-618, or narrow the comments to "bounds".
